mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost-push inflation, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive quarters, combined with a simultaneous drop in housing starts (HOUST), signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in personal income growth (implied by PAYEMS and GDPC1) outpacing consumer spending growth (RSAFS) creates a savings glut, which depresses short-term interest rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth exceeds RSAFS growth by >0.5pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when this condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) combined with rising CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) for six consecutive months signals a monetary policy lag, which erodes real equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.4 percentage points signals a sudden labor market shock, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) after such a shock.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained quarterly acceleration in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3% for two consecutive quarters signals improved macroeconomic fundamentals, which boost corporate earnings expectations and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during such quarters.
